key_insight: QMage proposes a coherent quantum search for crystalline materials whose Hamiltonian-derived properties meet specified targets within an error tolerance.
engineering_relevance: It could support first-principles materials discovery where classical property prediction is unreliable, but requires mature fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
method: Search over atomic compositions, unit cells, and atomic positions.
Block-encode each configuration’s Hamiltonian, isolate its target eigenstate, and evaluate properties coherently.
Use fixed-point quantum search to amplify and measure configurations satisfying the targets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports logical-qubit and Toffoli-depth estimates spanning a classically routine benchmark to harder targets, without numerical results or demonstrated speedups.
watch_item: Practical feasibility depends on the fault-tolerant resources needed for Hamiltonian encoding, eigenstate isolation, and property evaluation.
paper_title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
